basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome; acromesomelia 80-99%; functionally relevant visual abnormalities in roughly half or more. Singleton cardiac/renal reports do not establish common involvement.

decisions.ocular: involved: visual impairment, strabismus and refractive abnormalities affect roughly 50-80%; inclusion is not based on singleton optic atrophy alone.

basis: Peripheral demyelinating neuropathy; weakness and scoliosis are secondary to nerve dysfunction. Hearing and respiratory complications occur in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is annotated 30-79%, but is secondary to neuropathy; neurogenic weakness does not establish direct muscle or skeletal disease.

basis: Defining skin restriction, contractures and lung hypoplasia; oral restriction/cleft palate 80-99%. PDA/vascular anomalies and entropion (80-99%) omitted by cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none under cap: PDA/vascular anomalies are annotated 80-99%; severe oral restriction and palatal defects take priority for direct functional impairment.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: microstomia and cleft palate occur in 80-99%, with persistent oral structural and feeding impairment.

basis: Ataxia, immunodeficiency and cutaneous telangiectasia define disease; gonadal dysfunction/delayed puberty 80-99%. Eye movements are neurologic; liver enzymes alone insufficient.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent cutaneous telangiectasia is a defining diagnostic feature; the primary tier includes defining organs without requiring secondary functional damage.

basis: Heterotaxy with congenital heart defects; asplenia/hyposplenism affects roughly half across heterotaxy, with subtype uncertainty. Malrotation alone does not establish bowel dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: involved: absent or functionally deficient spleen occurs in roughly half of heterotaxy patients; this is organ loss, with limited subtype-specific frequency data.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: malrotation is common (~50-70%) but often asymptomatic; malposition alone is not damage, and volvulus is a minority complication.

basis: Defining urinary tract defects, absent abdominal musculature, pulmonic stenosis and intellectual disability retained. Defining deafness also qualifies but is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability is defining and retained; urinary, abdominal muscle and cardiac defects occupy the three primary slots.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital abdominal wall muscle deficiency is a defining component of prune belly, not secondary neurogenic weakness.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: defining deafness qualifies, but urinary tract, abdominal muscle, cardiac and neurodevelopmental disease take the four available slots.

basis: Glycosylation defect with defining severe neurodevelopmental disease; optic/retinal pathology and hearing loss each 1/1 assessed (at least 1/2 cases). Scoliosis 2/2 likely secondary to motor disease.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe developmental impairment and epilepsy in 2/2, with cortical atrophy, constitute the defining clinical phenotype.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic disc pallor and retinal vessel attenuation in 1/1 assessed support ocular pathology; cerebral visual impairment alone would be neurologic.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment in 1/1 assessed, representing at least 1/2 reported cases, meets the frequency threshold.

basis: Defining developmental delay, skeletal hypoplasia and obesity; mixed hearing impairment 1/2 (50%). Ptosis 2/2 omitted by cap: functional severity unspecified. Neonatal hypoglycemia is transient.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: ptosis occurs in 2/2, but its functional severity is unspecified; documented mixed hearing loss is prioritized.
decisions.otologic: involved: mixed hearing impairment in 1/2 (50%) is direct sensory organ dysfunction and is prioritized over ptosis of unspecified severity.

basis: Immune-mediated ulcerating dermatosis; direct extracutaneous myositis is rare (<30%) despite supplied annotation. Arthritis, IBD and marrow disorders are separate diseases.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: direct PG myositis is a rare extracutaneous manifestation (<30%); the 80-99% HPO annotation does not match the disease's usual course.

basis: Defining gonadal endocrine failure and sensorimotor neuropathy. Muscle atrophy (80-99%) is secondary to denervation; gonadoblastoma occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy is frequent (80-99%) but results from peripheral nerve loss, not direct disease of skeletal muscle.
